beats.say: Smart people don't work harder. They switch life from hard to easy.
Here are the seven laws they follow.
One. Kidlin's Law. A worry in your head is a tangle. Write down three issues: three deadlines, report not started, inbox full. Just writing it down can halve the problem.
beats.name: Kidlin's Law
beats.sub: Writing a problem down can halve it.

beats.say: Two. Pareto's Law. Of ten things you do, two drive eighty percent of the results. Do those first.
beats.name: Pareto's Law
beats.sub: About 80% of results come from 20% of the effort.

beats.say: Three. Murphy's Law. What can go wrong, will. So plan it once: if the train is late, I'll take the seven-forty.
beats.name: Murphy's Law
beats.sub: Anything that can go wrong, will. So prepare once.

beats.say: Four. Wilson's Law. Keep growing your knowledge and skills. Your earnings usually lag behind. Never forget that.
beats.name: Wilson's Law
beats.sub: Grow your knowledge and skills. Earnings lag behind.

beats.say: Five. Gilbert's Law. Your boss asks: can you sort out the client report? You can respond three ways. One, wait for instructions. Two, do just what's said. Three, propose the best way. Pick three. Working out the best way is the job.

data.prompt: Can you sort out the client report?

beats.name: Gilbert's Law
beats.sub: Working out the best way is part of the job.

beats.say: Six. Falkland's Law. Does this need deciding today? Yes? Decide, and move on. No? Wait, and let it get clearer.
beats.name: Falkland's Law
beats.sub: If you don't have to decide yet, don't.

beats.say: Seven. Hick's Law. Twenty-four options? Slow and doubtful. Three options? Fast and confident.
beats.name: Hick's Law
beats.sub: More options mean slower, less confident choices.

beats.say: Which law do you break most? Comment the number below.
